# Engineering Handbook

## 1. Ingestion

Document ingestion converts source files into normalized text records before downstream indexing. The loader must preserve useful content and attach stable source metadata.

## 2. Data quality

A reliable retrieval pipeline should handle ordinary prose, technical terminology, lists, tables, and documents with uneven text density without silently losing information.

## 3. Operations

Operational reports often contain timestamps, identifiers, measurements, and repeated headings. These elements are meaningful to users and should remain available after extraction.

## 4. Evaluation

The evaluation dataset uses fixed content and stable markers so that changes in extraction can be diagnosed independently from changes in chunking or retrieval.

## 5. Failure handling

A source document may be short, very long, multilingual, or structurally unusual. The ingestion layer should either process it predictably or report a clear and actionable error.
